reading.body:
Ben Cline's AI record is mostly money and cosponsorships: five Amazon PAC contributions, two Google NetPAC contributions, and one Meta PAC contribution, alongside four AI bill cosponsorships and four recorded votes.

The pattern is concentration on the money side. Amazon PAC appears five times between June 2025 and August 2026, for $1,000 to $2,500 each. Google NetPAC appears twice, in February and August 2026, at $2,000 each. Meta appears once, at $1,000. The contributions are small individually and spread across the largest AI-adjacent corporate PACs rather than any single donor.

The legislative record is narrower than the donor list. The four cosponsorships are all AI-specific: H.R. 6875, the AI OVERWATCH Act on export controls and high-risk actors, H.R. 8283 on model theft, H.R. 9914 on adversarial threats and security risks, and one further bill. The recorded votes are on suspension motions, which pass by design and rarely split the chamber, so a Yea or Nay there carries less signal than a vote on a contested rule.

What the data does not show is causation, and it does not claim any. Contributions and cosponsorships sit on the same timeline because the page places events in date order, not because one produced the other. It also does not cover committee assignments, floor statements, or amendments, which is where AI policy is often actually shaped. Nothing here speaks to data centers, power, or compute directly.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Ben Cline: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 15 events.
